擦.meaning: The ship's cook has lost her cheese grater, so she ties a block of cheese to the <part>anchor</part> and drags it along the rocky seabed. As it comes up, the crew <part>guess</part> how much is left: just a bag of fluffy shreds. A rocky sea is a fine way to <kanji>grate</kanji>.
擦.on: She also grates the peel of a <sound>sats</sound>uma over the top.
擦.kun: Then she rubs a little of the cheese onto a plate of <sound>su</sound>shi.

縛.meaning: A <part>tennis player</part> keeps losing because her socks slip down. Her coach, a retired chef, winds strong <part>thread</part> round her ankles, knees and waist like a holiday roast. She can only hop to the net, but nothing slips. He sure knows how to <kanji>truss</kanji>.
縛.on: He adds a belt with a huge <sound>buc</sound>kle, just in case.
縛.kun: Her opponent, a <sound>shee</sound>p, laughs so hard it drops its <sound>bu</sound>ttered toast.

冗.meaning: A kind aunt knits a <part>blanket</part> for her <part>table</part> so it won't catch cold, then a scarf for each leg, then four little hats and a hot water bottle. The table never asked for any of it. Every stitch is <kanji>superfluous</kanji>.
冗.on: A <sound>jo</sound>ey hops out of the pile wearing one of the hats.

渓.meaning: A puppeteer lowers her <part>marionette</part> on a string, metres and metres down between two cliffs, to fill its tiny bucket from the stream far below. Cold <part>water drops</part> splash its painted face. She's never needed so much string as for this deep <kanji>ravine</kanji>.
渓.on: At the bottom it finds a picnic: a slice of birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke on a rock.
渓.kun: It comes back up with a <sound>ta</sound>co balanced on one wooden <sound>knee</sound>.

塔.meaning: Every year a family stacks one more <part>picnic basket</part> on the same mound of <part>soil</part>, each with a curved, roof-shaped lid. After a century the stack is ten storeys high, with bells on every lid. Tourists climb it, sure it's a <kanji>pagoda</kanji>.
塔.on: A boy at the top balances on one big <sound>toe</sound> to ring the highest bell.

悠.meaning: A <part>fan seller</part> has kept the same stall on the same bridge for five hundred years. Kings, trams and shops come and go; his kind <part>heart</part> stays the same, and so does his price. He's less a man than a piece of <kanji>permanence</kanji>.
悠.on: His only customer as old as he is is a <sound>u</sound>nicorn, who buys one fan each century.

俺.meaning: In a rough biker bar, someone has hung a frilly pink <part>parasol</part> on the <part>coat hook</part>. 'Whose is this?' growls the barman. The biggest biker stands up, thumps his chest and says, 'Mine. <kanji>I</kanji> love it.'
俺.on: He rides off with it open above him, his <sound>en</sound>gine roaring.
俺.kun: An <sound>o</sound>tter rides behind him on the seat, holding a <sound>re</sound>d balloon.
